headline: Medium risk: shared customer-support workflows can leak data and create output-to-output cascades, while prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of a documented shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface external messages and integrations, while Rasa consumes conversational text via messaging channels. No shared filesystem or MCP bridge is documented, so the pathway is not default. The plausible bridge is manual or channel-based content passing, which keeps blast radius small but nonzero.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is manually copied into a Rasa training or runtime channel, injection becomes plausible.
IF an operator wires both agents to the same message queue or clipboard bridge, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste handoff between agents during triage.
Use a human review step before importing Chatwoot text into Rasa.
Separate channels so Chatwoot transcripts are not auto-fed to Rasa.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports, while Rasa handles text and voice. Both have network egress and customer-support use cases, so a shared workspace or forwarded transcript could expose sensitive support data to another processing path. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or reports are forwarded into Rasa inputs, customer data may leave the original support boundary.
IF both agents are deployed under the same workspace or account, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Rasa inputs to redacted text only.
Keep Chatwoot exports out of shared folders.
Review outbound integrations on both agents.
Turn off unnecessary logging for support transcripts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and multiple API integrations; Rasa has allowlisted egress and does not support multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because no shared write surface is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external ticketing or messaging endpoint, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource without locking, contention increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct outbound endpoints per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same ticket or thread.
Use a single writer for shared records.
Check integration scopes before enabling both agents.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate support messages and reports, and Rasa is a dialogue system that can consume text from channels. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input to Rasa, errors or hallucinated summaries can cascade into downstream responses. The profiles do not document verification between them, so the interaction is inferred.
conditions: IF Chatwoot summaries are fed into Rasa without human verification, downstream responses may repeat errors.
IF Rasa is configured to act on Chatwoot-generated text as ground truth, cascades become more likely.
mitigations: Require human review of Chatwoot summaries before reuse.
Mark Chatwoot-derived text as untrusted in Rasa.
Add validation rules for extracted facts.
Limit Rasa actions to low-risk replies.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot explicitly touches customer data and interaction history, while Rasa handles text and voice. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, logging, or residency if the pair is used on regulated support content. The profiles do not show certifications or residency guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are processed through both agents, retention and logging policies must align.
IF either deployment stores transcripts longer than the other, compliance mismatch arises.
mitigations: Compare retention settings for both agents.
Minimize stored transcript content.
Confirm residency and DPA coverage before use.
Review audit-log destinations.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems.
